#+title: Working with prepared native products

* A normal edit
Keep the compiler VM warm for source analysis and ordinary evaluation. Native
preparation happens when a product is needed. Application-only edits reuse the
native product; Rust and toolchain changes create a new one. The selected
library and each preparation's receipt make that distinction visible.

* Two people or two agent sessions
Each request has its own retained result. Identical Nix derivations can share
production without sharing a writable Cargo target. Session state and product
identity stay separate. A disconnected requester does not establish that a
shared daemon build was cancelled. Per-subscriber cancellation and durable job
reconnection need an explicit coordinator policy.

* A failed build
The error belongs to preparation. The old native selection stays usable.
Inspect the failed command's bounded log and compare the new source snapshot
with the working receipt. Keep an artifact capsule when reporting a successful
product whose runtime behavior fails a later test.

* A runtime update
Prepare the candidate first. Compare its identity, run the intended consumer
checks, then start a compatible fresh VM or use the runtime's supported code
activation protocol. Native libraries, in-VM generation ownership, serving
readiness and application-data migration are separate decisions.

* Capabilities and their delivery state
| Capability | Available surface | Scope |
| Immutable native preparation | artifacts prepare; artifact/prepare-native! | Standalone locked Linux x86_64 cdylib crates |
| Ordinary build integration | Normal checkout/build commands | Nix-only Source/runtime refresh and pinned prerequisites before BEAM |
| Authenticated command executor | Managed platform and automatic checkout staging | Exact helper digest/protocol checked before commands; no ambient Rust required |
| Managed build-host policy | nixosModules.artifacts | Strict sandbox and aggregate worker limits; apply and validate through host deployment |
| Explicit retention | Per-request Nix roots and receipts | Conservative retention; automatic live-consumer GC remains a separate gate |
| Product inspection | artifacts list | Stored successful receipts |
| Candidate comparison | artifacts compare | Identity changes; compatibility needs runtime checks |
| Reproduction descriptors | artifacts capsule | Verified artifact/source and runtime identities; test qualification stays explicit |
| Executable NIF showcase | examples/artifacts/showcase.bl | Real Rustler preparation and invocation |
| Environment preparation | Pinned recipe and platform lock | Rust/compiler/vendor closure; broader native system-dependency recipes need declared support |
| Shared production | Nix derivation identity | Independent clients/roots; durable subscription UI is coordinator work |
| Remote reuse | Existing Nix daemon configuration | Remote worker/target/cache trust requires environment qualification |
| Comparison realms | Exact product addresses are available | Realm orchestration and state isolation remain runtime integration work |
| Failure capsules with test replay | Artifact descriptor exists | Test selection/receipt attachment and replay UI remain integration work |
| Source-to-artifact impact explanations | Manifest comparison exists | Join language analysis and Nix dependency graphs in a later feature |
| Bounded production workers | Fixed-memory KVM guests and disk-backed scratch | Native/SDK workers are bounded; aggregate admission and cost-aware scheduling need their coordinator gates |
| Rollback | Prior artifacts remain retained | Activation, compatibility and data restore use the existing Foundry/runtime contracts |

* Boundaries that stay with the language
Compiler semantics, hygienic expansion, descriptor truth, execution admission,
actor/callback lifetimes and retirement of running code belong to Beam Lisp.
Nix supplies filesystem products. Foundry coordinates preparation and deployment.
Actual runtime loading and qualification determine what those products can do.
